matched_failure_patterns.label: Large-scale spectacle arrives before a specific vulnerable person/creature or relationship
matched_failure_patterns.archive_signal: Epic's diffuse Earthquake disaster montage underperformed creature-protection films; RIFTBORN/The Next Show lows also ask viewers to care about scale, realms, or journey mechanics before a person.
matched_failure_patterns.risk_logic: Destruction, armies, monsters, and world scale become noise when the audience does not yet know whom to protect or love.
matched_failure_patterns.mitigation: Within the first 90 seconds, tie spectacle to a visible vulnerable object and a protector's costly choice; make scale threaten someone specific.

matched_failure_patterns.label: Creature attack/chase spectacle begins early but never becomes a specific protection, family, or personhood relationship
matched_failure_patterns.archive_signal: Epicverse's low-performing giant snake/white ape short shows the snake almost immediately, but sampled middle/ending audio is mostly screams, roars, crashes, and combat; compare the giant-father hit where creature scale becomes paternal care.
matched_failure_patterns.risk_logic: Early creature action can falsify the slow-opening theory: spectacle may be immediate yet emotionally flat if victims are anonymous and the rescuer is only a combat asset.
matched_failure_patterns.mitigation: Give the creature or victim a specific relational role before the first chase ends; include a care/choice beat and make the ending transform belonging, trust, or personhood rather than only decide which monster wins.

positive_missing_or_weak: No strong hidden identity/secret hook detected; Nov Drama hits often use one, though this is not mandatory.
No child/heir/creature emotional anchor detected; this is currently one of the strongest archive-level positive signals.
No explicit status reversal detected in the surface promise.
No clear mythic creature lane detected; test whether the concept matches the channel audience's demand.
No specific relational/vulnerable anchor detected early; cross-channel evidence favors a visible child, creature, family member, lover, or protected person over abstract scale.
No early visual proof of the title/thumbnail promise detected; pay the premise in the opening movement rather than reserving it for the finale.
decision_guidance: Do not greenlight in current form; redesign the emotional engine or run a cheap validation artifact first.
Mitigate spectacle_scale_without_relational_anchor: Within the first 90 seconds, tie spectacle to a visible vulnerable object and a protector's costly choice; make scale threaten someone specific.

Mitigate creature_action_without_relational_bond: Give the creature or victim a specific relational role before the first chase ends; include a care/choice beat and make the ending transform belonging, trust, or personhood rather than only decide which monster wins.
failure_intelligence.causal_boundary: This is pattern-matching against public outcomes and extracted creative signals; it is not a causal predictor of CTR, retention, or audience response.

recommendations: Create legible injustice or danger within the first 90 seconds.
Pay the title/thumbnail fantasy visually by minute 5.
Treat compression as a completeness constraint: every scene should advance danger, bond, cost, or reversal in at least two ways.
Keep lore subordinate to a visible victim/protector relationship.
End with emotional belonging or safety, not only procedural victory, unless the asset is explicitly a serialized act with a next-problem hook.
format_strategy.causal_boundary: Duration/format guidance is observational and channel-dependent; it is not proof of retention or CTR causality.

meaning_carrier.opening_meaning: the key is a maintenance tool Noor uses as routine maintenance before the wreck
meaning_carrier.closing_reversal: the same key opens the foghorn line that drives the crab into the tide gate and frees trapped passengers
meaning_carrier.final_sequence_use: the object operates the final light/sound/trap mechanism before the rescued group reaches the dead lighthouse transformed into a sounding beacon guiding survivors and sea creatures home
warnings: meaning carrier ending recurrence cannot be verified without architecture sequences
meaning_carrier.craft_rule: A physical object, space, sound-object, or ritual should carry the wound in the opening and return with changed meaning in the payoff.

fields.power_asymmetry: predator-controlled terrain versus an injured professional with only knowledge, tools, and attention to vulnerable life
fields.safety_or_kindness_before_power: Noor frees or protects an injured seabird chick tangled in radio wire before knowing it can guide, prove, or save anyone
fields.costly_protagonist_action: she turns back toward the predator territory to free captives and an ancient leatherback turtle carrying moss and shell scars instead of escaping alone
fields.consent_or_personhood_repair: the allied creature is never commanded as a weapon; it chooses contact or return freely, and survivors repair their earlier dismissal of the animal
fields.payoff_image: the dead lighthouse transformed into a sounding beacon guiding survivors and sea creatures home; the turtle returns to open water with the seabird chick safe on its mossy shell

relational_contract.craft_rule: Power-asymmetric relationships are strongest when safety or costly kindness precedes power, and the ending repairs consent/personhood rather than rewarding coercion.

warnings: opening does not establish a legible spatial status grammar (who is caged, seated, kneeling, serving, or excluded)
spatial grammar lacks a clear vulnerable/powered social relation
spatial_status.doctrine: Define who is physically forced below/outside/inside power, then make the ending transform that space into chosen access, sanctuary, or belonging. Inspired by floor/table and cage/sanctuary evidence.
